For example, Mt Elbert’s official elevation was listed as [14,433 feet until 2002](http://www.skyrunner.com/story/coheights.htm), when the USGS released updated maps based on improved methodologies. They showed the peak was actually seven feet taller than previously thought, bringing the official elevation to 14,440 feet where it has remained ever since.
However, in 2021, analysts used new LIDAR technology to measure the peak’s elevation at 14,338 feet.

excerpts.text: Results: Mt Elbert summit is 14,439.45ft +/-0.04ft (NAD83 2011 Epoch 2010 NAVD88 Geoid 18)
In 1993 the USGS updated the vertical datum for the US to NAVD88, and this resulted in the elevation of Mt Elbert being shifted to 14,440ft, though no additional ground survey was conducted.
In 2021 USGS commissioned airplane-based LiDAR measurements to be taken over Colorado. These were analyzed to find an elevation of 14,438ft NAVD88 for the summit.
